docs.purpose: Registers a phone for push notifications by saving its device token against the signed-in user's account. Safe to call again — after an app reinstall, say — without creating duplicates.
docs.data_story: It touches no table at all and writes `device_tokens`. Its response shape is **unmeasured** as a pick-by-name whitelist — it passes rows through, spreads a row into a computed object, or assembles the payload dynamically, so there is no single list naming what leaves the server. It is called from 1 place: `mobile/src/lib/pushTokens.ts`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `MUTATION`. It declares `database.writes[]` with a `write_discipline` per target (the Spec 122 vocabulary verbatim), its idempotency posture, its optimistic contract and its rollback. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Response is a bare {success:true} acknowledgement with no data projection to measure. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: CENSUS AGREEMENT: census_reads [] and census_writes ['device_tokens'] both match — I read the file in full and there is exactly one SQL statement (route.ts:40-46) and no SELECT. Reviewer notes: (1) the route never de-registers or expires stale tokens, and has no rate limit, so device_tokens grows one row per distinct token string an authenticated client submits; (2) push_token has no max length (route.ts:16); (3) response shapes are bare, not the {data,error,meta} envelope, despite the withApiEnvelope wrapper. | Idempotency: Guarded. `ON CONFLICT (user_id, push_token) DO UPDATE SET updated_at = NOW(), platform = EXCLUDED.platform` (src/app/api/notifications/register/route.ts:43-44). A repeat POST with the same (user_id, push_token) updates rather than duplicating or 409-ing. No IS DISTINCT FROM guard, so `updated_at` moves on every replay even when `platform` is unchanged — which is the intended semantic here (last-seen heartbeat), not a defect. | Caching: none observed — no revalidate/dynamic/Cache-Control/unstable_cache in src/app/api/notifications/register/route.ts:1-53 | Other guards / classification: user_id is bound from the session (route.ts:45), never from the body — the body schema has no user_id field (route.ts:15-20). No rate limit: an authenticated client can register unbounded DISTINCT push_token values, each creating a new device_tokens row (the ON CONFLICT key is (user_id, push_token), route.ts:43, so distinct tokens do not collapse). | Locking tests: src/tests/notifications.infra.test.ts.
